# Enrich references with abstracts and quotations generated by Claude

You have PDFs linked to your references and want Citavi to contain an abstract and the most important quotations with page numbers, without copying them by hand.

## Solution
For each reference in the current selection, the macro sends the first linked PDF file to Claude, by default through a [LiteLLM](https://docs.litellm.ai) proxy. Claude reads the document (including scanned pages) and returns:

- an English **abstract**, which is written only if the reference's abstract field is empty
- up to 15 **direct quotations**, verbatim, with the printed page number (or the PDF page if no page number is printed) and an English core statement
- up to 8 **summaries** of the main sections, with page ranges

Existing abstracts and quotations are never changed. Quotations and summaries are only added if the reference has no quotations yet (highlights don't count). References that already have both an abstract and quotations are not sent to Claude at all, so the macro can safely be run again. All new quotations get the keyword `AI-generated` so that you can review them.

The limits, the model, and the keyword can be changed in the `EDIT HERE` section of the macro.

## Requirements
- A LiteLLM proxy with a Claude model that accepts PDF input. Set `model` (the model name in your LiteLLM config) in the `EDIT HERE` section.
- Two Windows user environment variables (Windows settings > "Edit environment variables for your account"), then restart Citavi:
  - `LITELLM_BASE_URL`: the base URL of the proxy, e.g. `https://litellm.example.com`
  - `LITELLM_API_KEY`: your LiteLLM key
- To call Anthropic directly instead, set `LITELLM_BASE_URL` to `https://api.anthropic.com` and `LITELLM_API_KEY` to an Anthropic API key.

## Important
- The PDF files are sent to the proxy and the model provider. Only use the macro if you are allowed to share the documents.
- Generated text can contain errors. Check quotations and page numbers against the PDF before citing them.
- Analysis can take several minutes per PDF. Citavi does not respond while the macro is running.
